reading.body:
Mercury Strategies filed 31 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI, and its largest AI clients are telecom carriers and their trade association.

The client list is concentrated: CTIA at 10 filings, Lumen at 8, then Verizon, AT&T and IAC at 4 each. That is 30 of the 31 filings held by this site, and it puts the firm's AI lobbying work squarely in communications infrastructure rather than in model developers or data centers. For AI specifically, the carriers are the companies that own the fiber, the backhaul and much of the physical plant that training and inference traffic runs over, so their legislative interests and AI policy interests overlap.

Three lobbyists carry the work: Andrew Fields and James Green on 31 filings each, Anne-Marie Kelley on 27. The bills named span both chambers, with eleven Senate bills and three House bills, all dated 2025 or later. The data does not say what position the firm or its clients took on any of them, and it does not link any bill to a compute, power or building provision.

summary: MERCURY STRATEGIES, LLC filed 31 Lobbying Disclosure Act reports on AI held by this site. Its clients, the lobbyists named on those filings and the AI bills they name are below. LDA registrant id 70131.
